2608.02491.title: Long-term Measurements: Towards a Longitudinal Understanding of Human-AI Interactions
2608.02491.paper_summary: Language models have taken on the role of a very new type of technology, by virtue of their "human-ness" and rapid integration into users' daily lives. This combination of features can introduce longitudinal risks---cognitive, developmental and socio-affective changes in humans---that might not surface in short-term interactions, but can have lasting long-term effects on users. This forms the basis of a critical new mission for NLP: to pivot from static, short-term evaluations of text generations to long-term measurements of behavioral changes, towards a diachronic understanding of human-model interactions. In this work, we draw from measurements used in social science fields that are crucial to understand emergent phenomena in longitudinal data. We discuss how computational methods in the field of NLP need to be combined with such measurements, not only to understand long-term safety risks of human-model interactions, but to help steer model development towards positive rather than negative outcomes for users. This ability to model human behavioral shifts as a function of model interactions can facilitate online rather than post-hoc detection of problematic behaviors, and should be leveraged in alignment frameworks to mitigate long-term risks in users.
2608.02491.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型因其「人性」及快速融入用戶日常生活而成為一種全新的技術。這些特徵的結合可能會引入縱向風險——人類的認知、發展和社會情感變化——這些風險在短期互動中可能不會顯現，但對用戶卻可能產生持久的長期影響。這為自然語言處理（NLP）提出了一項關鍵的新任務：從靜態的短期文本生成評估轉向對行為變化的長期測量，朝向對人類與模型互動的歷時理解。在這項工作中，我們借鑒了社會科學領域中用於理解縱向數據中新興現象的測量。我們討論了NLP領域中的計算方法如何需要與這些測量結合，不僅是為了理解人類與模型互動的長期安全風險，也是為了幫助引導模型發展朝向對用戶有利而非不利的結果。這種將人類行為變化建模為模型互動函數的能力，可以促進對問題行為的在線檢測，而不是事後檢測，並應在對齊框架中加以利用，以減輕用戶的長期風險。
